findings.detail: 3 of 9 active users have no 2SV. Org-wide enforcement starts 2026-02-10 (8 days): they will be locked out.
findings.recommendation: Chase enrollment (passkeys count only once 2SV is turned on), or suspend unused accounts.
findings.reference: CIS Google Workspace Foundations Benchmark: 2-Step Verification
findings.title: 3 active user(s) not enrolled in 2SV

findings.detail: Unconfigured third-party apps access level: ACCESS_LEVEL_UNSPECIFIED.
findings.recommendation: Security → API controls → Manage third-party app access: review the apps already used, mark the needed ones Trusted or Limited, then set unconfigured apps to 'Sign in with Google only' or block.
findings.reference: CIS Google Workspace Foundations Benchmark: API controls
findings.title: Any user can grant any third-party app access to company data

findings.detail: 4 distinct apps were authorized in the token audit window; 2 have full Gmail, full Drive or admin scopes.
evidence: Acme Mail Assistant: 2 user(s), mail.google.com (FULL GMAIL)
findings.recommendation: Review each app with its users; mark the needed ones Trusted or Limited and block the rest.
findings.reference: CIS Google Workspace Foundations Benchmark: API controls
findings.title: 2 third-party app(s) hold high-risk scopes

findings.detail: Google flagged these sign-ins or blocked sensitive actions.
findings.recommendation: Confirm each with the user; reset password and revoke sessions for anything unexplained.
findings.reference: Google Admin: Login audit log
findings.title: 1 suspicious sign-in or blocked risky-action event(s)

findings.detail: Travel and VPNs explain most of these; an admin account in this list deserves a direct check.
findings.recommendation: Ask each user to confirm; check Security → Alert center for related alerts.
findings.reference: Google Admin: Login audit log
findings.title: 1 account(s) signing in from several countries

findings.detail: SMS and voice codes can be phished or SIM-swapped.
findings.edition_note: Security-key-only enforcement is available on every edition.
findings.recommendation: Require security keys or passkeys at least for admins: put them in their own OU or group and set 'Only security key'.
findings.reference: CIS Google Workspace Foundations Benchmark: 2-Step Verification
findings.title: Any 2SV method is allowed, including SMS and voice codes

findings.detail: Dormant and shared mailboxes keep working passwords nobody watches.
findings.recommendation: Suspend or archive them, or convert shared mailboxes to Groups / delegated access.
findings.reference: CIS Google Workspace Foundations Benchmark: User account management
findings.title: 1 active account(s) with no sign-in for 90+ days

findings.detail: Domain-wide delegation lets a service account act as any user for the granted scopes.
findings.recommendation: Security → API controls → Domain-wide delegation: confirm each client and trim scopes.
findings.reference: CIS Google Workspace Foundations Benchmark: API controls
findings.title: 1 domain-wide delegation grant(s) in the audit window

findings.detail: Anyone who obtains the URL can open these files without signing in.
findings.recommendation: Ask owners to review drive_link_shared_full.csv; restrict links to the organization by default.
findings.reference: CIS Google Workspace Foundations Benchmark: Drive sharing
findings.title: 3 company-owned file(s) open to anyone with the link

findings.detail: 1 grant edit or higher rights; 1 go to personal mail domains.
findings.edition_note: Trust rules and Drive DLP are not available on Business Starter; use the standard sharing settings.
findings.recommendation: Review drive_external_shares.csv with owners; turn on the warning when sharing outside the organization; consider an allowlist of trusted domains.
findings.reference: CIS Google Workspace Foundations Benchmark: Drive sharing
findings.title: 3 sharing grant(s) to 3 outside domain(s)

findings.detail: Some protections are off, and others only show a warning banner.
findings.recommendation: Apps → Gmail → Safety → Spoofing and authentication: turn every check on and move suspicious mail to spam.
findings.reference: CIS Google Workspace Foundations Benchmark: Gmail safety
findings.title: Gmail spoofing and authentication protections are partial

findings.detail: Minimum length 8 (recommend 12+); requirements not enforced at next sign-in.
evidence: requirements not enforced at next sign-in
findings.recommendation: Security → Authentication → Password management: minimum 12, enforce at next sign-in.
findings.reference: CIS Google Workspace Foundations Benchmark: Password management
findings.title: Password policy is weaker than recommended

findings.detail: New shared drives allow: allowNonMemberAccess, allowExternalUserAccess.
findings.recommendation: Apps → Drive and Docs → Sharing settings → Shared drive creation: tighten the defaults.
findings.reference: CIS Google Workspace Foundations Benchmark: Drive sharing
findings.title: Shared drive defaults allow outside or non-member access

findings.detail: Users can sync company files to personal, unmanaged computers.
findings.edition_note: Restricting to authorized devices needs advanced endpoint management (Business Plus and above).
findings.recommendation: Restrict Drive for desktop to authorized devices where the edition allows it.
findings.reference: CIS Google Workspace Foundations Benchmark: Drive and Docs
findings.title: Drive for desktop works on any computer

findings.detail: Users can create or join spaces with any outside organization.
findings.recommendation: Apps → Google Chat → External Chat settings: restrict to allowlisted domains.
findings.reference: CIS Google Workspace Foundations Benchmark: Google Chat
findings.title: External Chat spaces are open to every domain

findings.detail: Owners can add external members; owners can accept mail from the public.
evidence: owners can accept mail from the public
findings.recommendation: Apps → Google Groups for Business → Sharing settings: keep groups internal.
findings.reference: CIS Google Workspace Foundations Benchmark: Groups for Business
findings.title: Google Groups can be opened to outsiders

findings.detail: Takeout lets any user download a full copy of their account data.
findings.recommendation: Apps → Additional Google services → Takeout: turn off for users who don't need it.
findings.reference: CIS Google Workspace Foundations Benchmark: Takeout
findings.title: Users can export data with Google Takeout

findings.detail: Without an enforcing DMARC policy, anyone can send mail that appears to come from your domain.
findings.recommendation: Publish SPF and DKIM, then move DMARC from p=none to quarantine and reject with rua= reports; add MTA-STS and TLS-RPT.
findings.reference: CIS Google Workspace Foundations Benchmark: Email authentication (SPF, DKIM, DMARC)
findings.title: Mail authentication DNS records are incomplete

findings.detail: Stale devices may still hold synced mail; unlocked ones expose it to anyone holding the phone.
findings.edition_note: Business Starter has basic mobile management only: no remote wipe of the whole device, no app management.
findings.recommendation: Remove stale devices from the account (Devices → Mobile), and require a screen lock.
findings.reference: CIS Google Workspace Foundations Benchmark: Mobile device management
findings.title: 1 stale, 1 unlocked, 0 compromised mobile device(s) of 3

findings.detail: Role assignments and authentication or app-access setting changes.
findings.recommendation: Confirm each change was intended and made by the expected admin.
findings.reference: Google Admin: Admin audit log
findings.title: 2 security-relevant admin change(s) in the audit window
